title: U.S. Senate · Louisiana

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Bill Cassidy (R), first elected in 2014, ran for re-election but placed third in the May 16, 2026 Republican primary with 24.8% of the vote, behind Julia Letlow (44.8%) and John Fleming (28.3%), and did not advance to the runoff. Letlow defeated Fleming 56.9%-43.1% in the June 27, 2026 Republican primary runoff. On the Democratic side, Jamie Davis defeated Gary Crockett 79.9%-20.1% in the June 27, 2026 primary runoff after neither candidate topped 50% in the May 16 primary, which also included Nick Albares.

candidates.name: Jamie Davis
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Gary Crockett in the June 27, 2026 Democratic primary runoff.
candidates.currentRole: Farmer; former Tensas Parish Police Juror (District 7, 2015–2019)

summary.text: Jamie Davis is a third-generation Louisiana farmer, small-business owner and public servant from Waterproof in Tensas Parish, who owns and operates his family's more-than-2,000-acre farm producing sorghum, corn, soybeans and cotton. He previously served on the Tensas Parish Police Jury and currently serves on the Louisiana Democratic State Central Committee. He is running for U.S. Senate on lowering the cost of living, expanding access to healthcare, and supporting public education.

background.text: Born in Houston, Texas; raised in the Louisiana Delta and attended public schools before studying electrical engineering at Louisiana State University.
Returned home to work at Davis Farms, founded by his father in 1977, which he now owns and operates.
Elected Police Juror for District 7 in Tensas Parish in 2015, serving four years and as Vice President of the Police Jury; ran for State Representative in District 21 in 2023.

priorities.text: Wants to lower the cost of living for working families through fair tax policies, affordable healthcare, housing and fair wages, including reversing tax policies he says favor large corporations over workers.

Says healthcare is a basic human need and supports maintaining Affordable Care Act subsidies, protecting Medicaid access, lowering prescription drug prices and creating a Medicare option available to all Americans.
Supports strong public schools, competitive teacher pay and affordable access to college and vocational training.

positions.summary: Supports maintaining Affordable Care Act subsidies, protecting Medicaid access and creating a Medicare option available to all Americans.
Supports reversing tax policies he says favor large corporations over workers as part of lowering costs for working families.
Says he supports "practical immigration reform that combines lawful enforcement with humane policies."
Lists fair wages, alongside fair tax policies and affordable healthcare and housing, as a priority for lowering the cost of living.

candidates.name: Julia Letlow
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated John Fleming in the June 27, 2026 Republican primary runoff, after defeating incumbent Sen. Bill Cassidy and Mark Spencer in the May 16, 2026 primary.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 5th Congressional District (since 2021)

summary.text: Julia Letlow is the U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 5th Congressional District, elected in a 2021 special election after the death of her husband, Luke Letlow, who had won the seat but died before taking office. She is the first Republican woman elected to Congress from Louisiana. She is running for U.S. Senate with an endorsement from President Trump, campaigning on her record supporting law enforcement, workforce development and infrastructure funding for the district and on protecting parental rights in education.

background.text: Native of Monroe, Louisiana; earned a bachelor's and master's degree from the University of Louisiana Monroe and a doctorate in communication from the University of South Florida.

Worked as a university administrator and educator, including as executive director of external affairs and strategic communications at ULM (2018–2019) and in education and patient-safety roles at the Tulane University School of Medicine.

Took office in April 2021 after winning a special election with 65% of the vote for the seat her husband Luke Letlow had won but did not take due to his death from COVID-19 complications; serves on the House Committee on Appropriations and the House Committee on Education and the Workforce.

priorities.text: Campaigning as a conservative candidate with President Trump's endorsement, saying Louisiana "deserves a conservative Senator who will not waver."
priorities.quote: Today, I am announcing my candidacy for the United States Senate to ensure the nation we leave our children is safer and stronger. Louisiana deserves a conservative Senator who will not waver. I am honored to have President Trump's endorsement and trust.

priorities.text: Points to her House record of securing more than $130 million in targeted support for Louisiana for law enforcement, workforce development and infrastructure.
priorities.quote: In her time representing the 5th District, she has fought for conservative values and secured over $130 million in targeted support for Louisiana - supporting law enforcement, workforce development, and real infrastructure needs.

priorities.text: Says she has been a leader on protecting parents' rights in education and returning local control to the classroom.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations (Subcommittees on Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration; Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education; and National Security and the Department of State) and the House Committee on Education and the Workforce.
